title: "Problem Formulation"

---

**Study reference:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning*, §9.1. The examples, reasoning and notation explanations are written independently.

## Start from a problem

We want to predict minutes required for a new order using distance d and item count n. The first design decision is the feature vector and loss function—not the optimiser.

## Formulate the problem mathematically

$$
\hat y_i=\beta_0+\beta_1d_i+\beta_2n_i,\qquad L(\boldsymbol\beta)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}(y_i-\hat y_i)^2
$$

This relation identifies the required structure. Interpret the symbols using the stated model rather than memorising the formula without its assumptions.

## Derive a worked result

The six invented orders have feature rows (1,d_i,n_i) and times (7,12,11,18,17,22). For beta=(3,2,2), the first order predicts seven minutes exactly; the second predicts eleven versus observed twelve, contributing one unit of squared error.

## Why the mathematics matters

The columns form X∈R^{6×3}, beta∈R³ and y∈R⁶. The linearity is in coefficients, even if engineered input features later contain squares or interactions. Prediction is not a causal claim about what changing distance would do.

## Explain or calculate

Write X for the first three orders and compute the three predictions under beta=(3,2,2).
